answer: Verdict: normalisation is real but not complete. The low FY25 impairment charge ($424m, 5bps of average loans, down from $537m/7bps in FY24) is genuinely earned: stressed exposures to TCE fell to 1.28% from 1.45%, mortgage 90+ delinquencies fell to 0.70% from 1.05%, and other consumer 90+ delinquencies fell to 1.08% from 1.40%. But the fall in the P&L charge came mainly from write-backs/recoveries nearly doubling and new IAPs shrinking, not from lower realised losses -- net write-offs to average loans actually rose 1bp to 6bps. On the balance sheet, the total ECL provision stock fell only 2% to $4,987m (from $5,096m a year earlier), because improving economics cut modelled CAP by $168m but a 5-percentage-point shift of scenario weight from upside (5.0% to 2.5%) into downside (42.5% to 47.5%) plus a $59m rise in overlays (to $238m) clawed most of that back. Westpac's own investor pack quantifies this caution directly: reported probability-weighted ECL of $4,987m sits $1.9bn above a hypothetical 100%-base-case ECL of $3,040m, though it remains well below a 100%-downside ECL of $7,152m. Coverage ratios are nonetheless drifting down (CAP/credit RWA 125bps vs 130bps a year ago; total provisions/gross loans 58bps vs 63bps), so the buffer is thinning at the margin even as its downside-weighting rises. Net: credit-risk normalisation is progressing, but the September 2025 provision stock still embeds roughly $1.9bn of stated caution above pure base-case modelling -- it is not evidence that normalisation is complete.

key_facts.fact: Total provision for ECL fell 2% to $4,987m at 30 Sept 2025 from $5,096m a year earlier (and from $5,072m at 31 March 2025), comprising collectively assessed provisions of $4,439m (modelled $4,201m plus overlays $238m) and individually assessed provisions of $539m.

Portfolio overlays rose to $238m at 30 Sept 2025 from $130m at 31 March 2025 and $179m at 30 Sept 2024, driven by new overlays for portfolio seasoning and higher-stress geographies, partly offset by releases in mortgages and consumer finance.

key_facts.fact: Management's own summary frames the provision stock as still cautious, stating that over the year the reduction in provisions from improved credit quality was more than offset in part by an increase in the downside scenario weight and higher overlays.

citations.quote: We remain appropriately provisioned with credit impairment provisions of $4,987 million. The ratio of collectively assessed provisions to credit RWA was 1.25%. Over the year provisions decreased by 2% with the reduction from improvements in credit quality more than offsetting an increase in the downside scenario weight and higher overlays.

limitations: The documents do not disclose the dollar composition of the $238m overlay balance by driver (seasoning, geography, sector releases) -- only qualitative descriptions are given, so the split within overlays cannot be verified.
Scenario weightings (upside/base/downside) are disclosed only at Group level; no segment-level or portfolio-level scenario weighting breakdown is provided.

No pre-COVID or longer-run average coverage ratio (CAP/credit RWA, total provisions/gross loans) is disclosed, so whether the current 125bps/58bps levels are high or low relative to history cannot be assessed from these two documents alone.

The $1.9bn 'provisions above base case' figure is a rounded chart annotation in the investor pack, not a reconciled note; the calculation methodology behind the 100%-downside ECL scenario figure ($7,152m) is not disclosed.

The presentation states the base-case/downside macro forecasts are dated 18 September 2025, which may predate the balance date (30 September 2025) by about two weeks; no update between those dates is disclosed.
